One must count edges (\u230aM/2\u230b) versus vertices (n+1) to find an acyclic component, then 2-colour it to get the signs, so that unmatched parts and the ±\u03b5_i telescoping give the bound. This is the only place where K \u2264 n enters; without it the claim is false, so it cannot be dismissed as routine.", "quote": "there is a set $V_T\\subseteq\\{0,\\dots,n\\}$ and signs $s:V_T\\to\\{\\pm1\\}$ such that the signed sum $\\Xi:=\\sum_{j\\in V_T}s(j)\\,q_j$ satisfies $|\\Xi|\\le\\sum_i\\varepsilon_i+[M\\text{ odd}]\\,a_M$ (standard; details omitted)"}, {"description": "Numerical/Monte-Carlo verification is repeatedly cited as support (for the answer, Lemma 4 and Lemma 5).
